title: Draft: Deprecate "ws_in4_addr" typedef
description:
Deprecated this type. It is confusing because it is never completely
obvious the byte order being used, despite being network byte order
by convention, and there are many uses of ws_in4_addr that look
wrong or at least dubious. The name also lacks the "_t" suffix
that is conventionally used.

Rename it to ws_in4h_addr_t, the extra "h" standing for host byte-order.
This way the byte order used or expected should never be in question.

We use host byte order because it is useful internally. Network byte
order is only relevant when interfacing with the C library, and those
situations are few and far between.

This is part of an effort to remove IPv4 address variables and argument declarations
everywhere as integers.
